value.body: A national research organisation under the Ministry of Culture, with headquarters in Kolkata and regional centres in different parts of the country. It studies India's populations — communities, cultures and human biology — and maintains anthropological collections and museums.

items.label: Parent ministry
items.value: Ministry of Culture, Government of India

items.label: Typical eligibility
items.value: Master's in anthropology for research posts
items.note: Some posts and fellowships also ask for NET or research experience

items.label: Regional centres
items.note: Dehradun, Mysuru, Udaipur, Shillong, Nagpur, Port Blair and an Eastern Regional Centre in Kolkata; a sub-regional centre at Jagdalpur

items.label: Postgraduate students in anthropology
items.note: Enrolment at PG level; ~430 more at Ph.D. level
items.source: AISHE (Ministry of Education) 2023-24, Table 13 (based on actual responses)

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Regular scientific posts (for example, assistant anthropologist) are filled through recruitment notices, including through UPSC. AnSI also advertises research fellowships and contract research posts directly. Openings are few and irregular; a master's in anthropology is the usual base requirement, so read each notice for the exact degree and specialisation asked for.

value.title: At a glance
items: A small employer — vacancies come up rarely.
State tribal research institutes and museums also employ anthropology postgraduates, usually through their own notices.
A Ph.D. or fieldwork experience helps for research posts.

value.title: Postgraduate enrolment in anthropology
value.note: Counts only institutions that responded to AISHE, so totals are approximate. This is the pool of anthropology postgraduates, not AnSI posts.
value.source: AISHE reports 2021-22, 2022-23 and 2023-24 (Ministry of Education), Table 13 — Anthropology, PG level
